messages.subject: Re: really confusing error when leaving out fill component of stacked bar: object y not found
parts:
Hi Steve -

The error messages from geom_bar can be confusing, because sometimes
it bins the data (counting the number of cases in each condition) and
sometimes it uses the specified y values.

I've filed an issue here:
https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/issues/632

-Winston


On Tue, Jul 24, 2012 at 12:04 PM, Steve Powell <st...@promente.net> wrote:
> Hi all
> the right way to make a single stacked bar from a dataframe which lists the
> values for the bar segments is this, according to
> http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/coord_polar.html
>
> library(ggplot2)
> df <- data.frame( variable = c("resembles", "does not resemble"), value =
> c(80, 20) )
> ggplot(df, aes(x = "", y = value, fill = variable)) + geom_bar(width = 1)
>
> I guess lots of folk especially beginners want this kind of thing,
> especially as it is a step to building a corresponding pie chart. Just now I
> was trying to remember the steps and did something like this instead:
>
> ggplot(df, aes(x = "", y = value)) + geom_bar(width = 1)
>
> i.e. the same but without the fill - and I get the error "Error in pmin(y,
> 0) : object 'y' not found"
> Sure I made a mistake, but I just think the error message is totally
> unhelpful - because of the message it then took me ages to fix because I was
> trying to work out why the y wasn't found. Just wondering if there is any
> clever way to understand the error?
>
> Best
> Steve
